mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT at t-0w signals renewed daytime circulation that should spill into retail visits within four weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC above its last-4-week average.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not remain above their t-1w levels for at least two consecutive weeks, and RETAIL_REC still fails to rise relative to the prior 4 weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays below roughly -50 percent for another week, commuter access remains constrained and retail trips stay suppressed over the next two weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC below its recent mean.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if TRANSIT rises above -50 and RETAIL_REC still does not improve over the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in RESIDENTIAL and rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more out-of-home errand activity and shorter home-stay time, which should translate into slightly higher retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while GROCERY_PHARM falls back, and RETAIL_REC does not rise in the next 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a prior trough is a proxy for improved weather and leisure propensity; that leisure spillover should lift retail-and-recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points from the prior week after a trough
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -48.7 at t-1w to -23.6 at t-0w after being -31.0 at t-2w
failure_condition: If PARKS does not sustain its rebound for two weeks and RETAIL_REC remains below the last-4-week average, the seasonal spillover claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in WORKPLACES together with a decline in TRANSIT signals weaker weekday movement; that combination should reduce incidental shopping trips and push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover meaningfully but RETAIL_REC still falls, then the causal link from weekday mobility to retail mobility is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM normalizes toward zero while WORKPLACES remains far below baseline, essential trips are being satisfied without broader re-entry to public life, so retail mobility stays subdued over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -10 while WORKPLACES stays below -20
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM improves above -10 and WORKPLACES remains below -20 but RETAIL_REC rises instead of falling, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in RESIDENTIAL indicates households are spending more time at home, which mechanically reduces discretionary retail outings and should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls back toward baseline and RETAIL_REC still declines, the home-stay suppression mechanism is not supported.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve from deeply negative levels and PARKS also rebounds, the combined easing of movement constraints should create a broader reopening signal that lifts retail-and-recreation mobility within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -50 and WORKPLACES rises above -30 while PARKS stays above -30
failure_condition: If the three proxies satisfy the improvement condition but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its previous 4-week mean, the reopening mechanism is rejected.
